stem: A door supervisor sees a man grab a customer's phone and run towards the exit. Which condition allows the door supervisor to arrest him without a warrant?
options: He is behaving in a way the operative finds offensive
He is in the act of committing an indictable offence
He has committed a minor motoring offence
The operative believes he may commit an offence next week
explanation: PACE section 24A allows a person other than a constable to arrest someone in the act of committing an indictable offence, or whom they reasonably suspect of doing so. The other options are not indictable offences being committed now.
source_quote: anyone who is in the act of committing an indictable offence

stem: A man suspected of an indictable offence is sitting calmly on a bench. Police are two minutes away. What else must be true before the operative may arrest him?
options: A constable cannot reasonably make the arrest instead
The man agrees to be arrested
The man has no identification
The operative has a written warrant
explanation: PACE section 24A also requires that it appears to the person making the arrest that it is not reasonably practicable for a constable to make the arrest instead.
source_quote: it is not reasonably practicable for a constable to make it instead

stem: During a fight, an operative pulls a man away to stop him punching someone. Which statement correctly describes the force the operative may use?
options: Any force needed to make the man leave the venue
Force only after a court has approved it
Force that is reasonable in the circumstances to prevent crime
No force at all, because only the police may use force
explanation: Section 3 of the Criminal Law Act 1967 allows a person to use such force as is reasonable in the circumstances in the prevention of crime or in making a lawful arrest.
source_quote: such force as is reasonable in the circumstances in the prevention of crime

stem: A security company sends a new operative to a busy venue without any site training or written instructions. Which employer duty has most directly not been met?
options: Providing the necessary information, instruction, training and supervision
Providing free meals during shifts
Paying the operative's travel costs
Checking the operative's licence with the SIA
explanation: HSWA section 2 places a duty on employers to provide the information, instruction, training and supervision necessary for the health and safety of employees, so far as is reasonably practicable.
source_quote: the provision of such information, instruction, training and supervision as is necessary

stem: A lone worker at a remote gate is told to check in by radio every hour. He skips the checks because nothing has ever happened. Which duty is he failing?
options: To carry out the employer's fire risk assessment
To provide his own first-aid training
To take reasonable care for his own health and safety and co-operate with his employer
To report the employer to the enforcing authority
explanation: HSWA section 7 requires every employee to take reasonable care for their own health and safety and that of others, and to co-operate with the employer's health and safety arrangements. Lone-worker check-ins are part of those arrangements.
source_quote: to take reasonable care for the health and safety of himself and of other persons

stem: An operative is first to reach a customer who has collapsed near a spilled chemical. What should the operative do first?
options: Move the customer away immediately
Start chest compressions
Give the customer water
Assess the situation and make the area safe without putting himself in danger
explanation: HSE first-aid priorities are to assess the situation without putting yourself in danger, make the area safe, then assess casualties and send for help.
source_quote: assess the situation – do not put yourself in danger

stem: An operative finds a customer who does not respond when asked loudly if they are all right. What should the operative do next?
options: Shout for help, open the airway and check for normal breathing
Start chest compressions straight away
Place the customer in the recovery position
Wait for the customer to wake up
explanation: HSE guidance says that if there is no response, the priorities are to shout for help, open the airway, check for normal breathing and then take appropriate action.
source_quote: shout for help; open the airway; check for normal breathing

stem: A storeroom has cardboard boxes stacked against a wall heater. Which fire prevention control does HSE guidance recommend?
options: Store the boxes in a locked cupboard under the stairs
Keep sources of ignition and flammable substances apart
Turn the heater off only at the end of the week
Ask staff to report fires after they start
explanation: HSE fire prevention guidance says to keep sources of ignition and flammable substances apart, and to avoid build-up of rubbish that could burn.
source_quote: keep sources of ignition and flammable substances apart

stem: A manager asks how long the current national threat level will last. What is the correct answer?
options: It expires after 30 days
It is reviewed only after an attack
It has no expiry date and can change at any time
It remains fixed until the next general election
explanation: Threat levels do not have an expiry date. They are set by the Joint Terrorism Analysis Centre and MI5 and can change at any time as information becomes available.
source_quote: Threat levels do not have an expiry date.

stem: A venue's written policy says that people of a certain nationality will not be allowed in. Which type of discrimination does this policy show?
options: Indirect discrimination
Victimisation
Harassment
Direct discrimination
explanation: Under Equality Act 2010 section 13, direct discrimination is treating someone less favourably because of a protected characteristic, such as race or nationality.
source_quote: A treats B less favourably than A treats or would treat others

stem: An operative clears out a store room and puts old incident logbooks, containing customers' names and addresses, into the general waste. What should have been done instead?
options: Dispose of paper and electronic waste securely
Keep the logbooks for at least ten years
Store the logbooks on a personal phone
Give the logbooks to another operative
explanation: ICO security guidance says physical security includes how you dispose of any paper and electronic waste, because hard-copy records can be lost, stolen or incorrectly disposed of.
source_quote: how you dispose of any paper and electronic waste

stem: Which of these is listed as a Class A controlled drug in Schedule 2 to the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971?
options: Amphetamine
Cocaine
Diazepam
Ketamine
explanation: Cocaine is listed in Part I of Schedule 2 as a Class A controlled drug.
